key_insight: ExCal detects multivariate time series anomalies without gradient optimization or anomaly labels by combining complementary expert scores calibrated against normal training data.
engineering_relevance: ExCal offers an optimization-free detection pipeline, but sequence-wide scoring makes the evaluated method suitable for batch analysis rather than online monitoring.
method: Fit raw-state retrieval memories, signal/derivative projections, and robust statistics across temporal scales.
Calibrate each expert with a high normality floor from the training prefix and retain positive excess.
Attenuate broadly firing experts and combine excess magnitudes with a small rank term.
evidence_signal: Across 180 series from 17 TSB-AD-M families and three seeds, ExCal ranked second among 24 methods with AUC-PR 0.421 ± 0.37 and VUS-PR 0.452 ± 0.37; Holm-adjusted paired tests found no significant difference from AxonAD or StreamVAE.
watch_item: Prevalence and ranks use the complete scored sequence; online suitability and the diagnostic utility of expert-level decomposition remain untested.
paper_title: ExCal: Optimization-Free Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection via Excess Calibration
